title: POC weekly — telemetry, credentialing, and fallback plan

Discussed minor regression in tail latency on long-context prompts and next steps for KV cache tuning and telemetry dashboards.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-18
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Nina Lopez (CSM), Priya Rao (Helio Head of AI), Jamie Chen (Platform Eng), Marcus Li (SecOps)

Auto-summary: Telemetry shows a small tail-latency regression on long-context prompts; creds mostly provisioned but KMS policy needs one tweak; VPC peering intermittent due to firewall rules; action items agreed.

[00:00] Alex (AE): ok hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we have — we have 42 minutes on the calendar, so we'll be pretty focused. quick roll call?
[00:08] Priya: hey priya here, thanks alex. jamie and marcus are on as well.
[00:12] Jamie: yep hi all.
[00:14] Marcus: marcus on secops.
[00:16] Samir (SE): sam here from the eng side at redwood. we'll jump into telemetry first.
[00:20] Alex: cool, nina, feel free to add anything from the cs side.
[00:23] Nina: nothing major, just i'll track follow-ups.

[02:00] Samir (SE): ok so the run from last night — we ingested the telemetry you pushed into the staging collector, thanks — overall token throughput looks fine, good QPS for 8k tokens but we did see a 95th/99th tail uptick when you hit prompts above 12k tokens.
[02:15] Priya: yeah we saw that too in our app logs, occasional 300–400ms spikes over the expected latency for those long chats. how confident are you that it's runtime vs network?
[02:30] Samir: initial triage points at KV cache cold misses on those very long chains; when the KV cache misses, the model ends up re-evaluating more context which increases decode time. we also saw a few extra round trips due to prefix merging.
[02:48] Jamie: hmm, we're using their default http keepalive; could it be an idle timeout? our infra team set a 60s idle close, maybe that's interfering with continuous streaming.
[03:05] Marcus: secops question — are tokens logged in plain text in telemetry? i saw a field that looks like a prompt snippet. we need to make sure pii isn't leaking.
[03:20] Alex: good call — by default we redact full prompt text in the telemetry export; what you probably saw are the truncated prompt hashes or the first 50 chars if you enabled debug. i'll confirm which export you have access to.
[03:36] Marcus: okay please confirm — compliance team will need that.

[05:00] Priya: another item — we still haven't had the KMS handoff finalized; we created a key but our policy complains about the principal. jamie, you saw that?
[05:12] Jamie: yes, the role arn we used in our test policy didn't include the redwood service principal format. we updated it, but iam isn't giving access during the peering test.
[05:24] Samir: we have a recommended policy snippet in the security pack, but small mismatch does happen — can you paste the current policy?
[05:33] Jamie: i'll paste in the chat after this call.

[07:00] Alex: ok onto vpc peering: we had two failed peering attempts overnight from what our networking logs show. one was blocked by a firewall rule that dropped 443 from the redwood egress. jamie is that the rule you mentioned?
[07:15] Jamie: yes, it looks like our egress-NAT rules didn't include the redwood-managed range. adding it resolved some of the tests but a new test flagged another subnet. it's a little piecemeal.
[07:30] Marcus: that's expected, our network is fairly locked down in prod, and staging mirrors some of that. we want to be explicit which cidrs to allow.
[07:42] Alex: we can send a minimized list of IP ranges and a small port matrix — that'll make it easier for your firewall team. we'll also provide a documented fallback port mapping for the hosted endpoint if direct peering fails.

[09:00] Priya: on the fallback idea — how disruptive is falling back to hosted in terms of auth and metrics? we can't afford big gaps in observability.
[09:13] Samir: two main impacts: 1) auth will swap to API-key based token issuance unless you route through our private tunnel, and 2) metrics tagging will still be available but some network-level traces (VPC flow logs correlation) will be lost. we'll, we will record request ids so you can stitch requests later but yeah there is some loss on the flow-level observability.
[09:40] Priya: ok that's helpful, we need the runbook text for security to review.

[12:00] Jamie: re: KV cache tuning — can you explain prefix caching vs full context caching? i've read the doc but want the plain english tradeoff.
[12:12] Samir: sure — prefix caching stores the commonly reused prompt prefixes (like system messages, instruction templates) as cached tensors; full context caching tries to cache larger contiguous sequences which reduces recompute at the cost of more memory and risk of cache fragmentation. for your long chat flows, prefix caching often gives a nicer latency/cost sweet spot.
[12:36] Jamie: ok and what's the plan to test it?
[12:40] Samir: we'll run a targeted benchmark replay using your provided 2-hour peak trace — enable prefix caching + keep KV warm with steady synthetic traffic. we'll measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost delta.

[15:00] Marcus: another security ask — audit logs retention. do you keep request-level logs for 90 days? our audit requirements say 90 days for specific endpoints.
[15:12] Alex: by default we keep request metadata 30 days in the telemetry service, but enterprise add-on can extend to 365; we can configure 90 days for the pilot under the compliance package. i'll attach the license note.
[15:30] Marcus: good. also, is data encrypted at rest with our KMS?
[15:36] Alex: yes data at rest is envelope-encrypted using your customer-managed KMS once you enable private mode; if you're in hosted default mode we use Redwood-managed keys. for the pilot you can opt in to customer KMS.

[18:00] Priya: pricing question — if we enable prefix caching and that drops token costs, does your billing reflect the lower decode token counts immediately or is there a lag?
[18:12] Alex: billing is based on observed tokens processed per request; if the cache reduces tokens at decode time that will show up in usage the next billing cycle, but you can also request a mid-pilot estimate.

[20:00] Jamie: one weird log we saw — a handful of streams showed 'certificate verify failed' in the agent logs. i think it's due to our proxy doing SNI rewriting.
[20:12] Samir: oh yes we've seen that when mutating proxies rewrite SNI or strip TLS headers. for now we recommend bypassing TLS inspection for redwood endpoints or adding our CA to the proxy trust store.
[20:30] Marcus: ok we'll test adding the CA on a dev box.

[22:00] Alex: quick note on the telemetry dashboard — nina can demo it next week, it has a long-context filter and a new tail-latency chart. can we get your preferred dashboard users?
[22:12] Nina: if you can give me the list of emails i will invite them.
[22:18] Priya: add me, jamie, marcus, plus two folks from analytics: carla and ryan.

[24:00] Samir: regarding the regression — we ran a micro-optimization last week that changed kernel selection for sequence lengths > 8k; in lab it shaved p50 but slightly increased p99 for pathological patterns. plan: revert to previous kernel for the pilot until we can test with your replay.
[24:24] Priya: that makes sense — we'd rather stable p99 for now. please revert.
[24:30] Samir: i'll revert and push a note to the runbook.

[27:00] Jamie: are there any changes to the API surface if we fallback to hosted? like parameter names or response shapes?
[27:12] Alex: no shape changes; we keep the same API contract. there is a minor header that indicates origin (x-rd-origin) so you can filter metrics, but payloads are stable.

[30:00] Marcus: security review reminder — we need the incident response blurb showing retained logs and notification SLA. can you include that in the security pack?
[30:12] Alex: yes i'll include the IR blurb and the notification SLA (we notify within 1 hour for severity 1 incidents).

[33:00] Priya: timeline check — our goal is a pilot go/no-go decision by end of month. are the actions here sufficient to hit that?
[33:12] Alex: yes if we get the KV tuning results and VPC peering confirmed this week we should have the perf numbers to evaluate.
[33:24] Nina: i'll collate items and send a status note mid-week.

[35:00] Samir: one technical note about telemetry retention — when using customer KMS we rotate the telemetry blobs under your key, which adds a decryption step in our ingest pipeline; that can add small latency to ingestion but not to inference. just flagging it.
[35:20] Marcus: ok that's fine, just annotate it in the doc.

[37:00] Alex: all right let's recap next steps — samir to run KV prefix caching test friday, i'll send SOC2 and the firewall CIDR list, jamie to confirm firewall updates, marcus to validate KMS policy, nina to schedule telemetry demo.
[37:20] Priya: agreed. also, please include the fallback runbook.
[37:28] Alex: yes we'll attach the runbook in the email.

[40:00] Jamie: quick logistics — can we get a 30-minute follow-up after the KV test? say monday morning?
[40:12] Nina: monday 09:00 UTC works for us, i'll send a calendar invite.
[40:20] Priya: that's good.

[41:30] Alex: thanks everyone. end notes: links we will share — security pack (link), minimal CIDR list (link), KV tuning script and expected outputs (link).
[41:50] Marcus: thanks all.
[42:00] Meeting end.
